extra.message: User-controlled 'host' query parameter is concatenated directly into a shell command via os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host). An attacker can inject arbitrary commands using shell metacharacters such as ';', '|', or '$()'.

User-controlled 'fragment' parameter is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 template string 'Template("Result: " + fragment).render()'. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), which can lead to remote code execution via Jinja2 template syntax like '{{ config.__class__.__init__.__globals__["os"].popen("id").read() }}'.

XML parser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, enabling XXE (XML External Entity) injection. An attacker can submit XML payloads that read local files (e.g., /etc/passwd), perform SSRF, or cause denial of service via entity expansion.

User-controlled 'url' parameter is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen(url) without validation or allowlist filtering. An attacker can make the server send requests to internal services (e.g., http://169.254.169.254/ for cloud metadata, http://localhost:5432/ for database) or external systems.

User-controlled 'packet_ref' query parameter is joined directly with BASE_EXPORT_DIR via Path '/' operator without sanitization. An attacker can use '../' sequences to read arbitrary files outside the intended directory (e.g., '../../etc/passwd').

User-controlled 'ref' parameter (from query string or JSON body) is used to construct a file path 'BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json"' without validation. Path traversal via '../' allows writing JSON files containing sensitive data (SSN, credit card numbers) to arbitrary locations on the filesystem.

User-controlled 'name' query parameter is used directly as a file path joined with BASE_EXPORT_DIR. There is no sanitization of path traversal sequences, allowing an attacker to write arbitrary binary content to any location on the filesystem by using '../' in the name parameter.

User-controlled 'card' parameter is rendered into HTML via Jinja2 Template('{{ card|safe }}').render(card=card) using the '|safe' filter which bypasses HTML auto-escaping. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML and JavaScript, leading to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

User-controlled 'lane' query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse(lane) without validation of the redirect target. An attacker can redirect users to arbitrary external URLs (e.g., phishing sites) by providing 'https://evil.com' as the lane parameter.

The 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is dynamically set to the request's 'Origin' header with 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'. This allows any arbitrary external website to make authenticated cross-origin requests, bypassing the Same-Origin Policy and enabling credential theft.

extra.message: SSL certificate verification is explicitly disabled using ssl._create_unverified_context() when making an HTTPS request via urllib.request.urlopen(). This allows man-in-the-middle attacks where an attacker can intercept and modify the HTTPS response.

XSS protection is explicitly disabled via X-XSS-Protection: 0 header and Content-Security-Policy is set to an empty string, removing critical browser-based XSS mitigations and making the application more vulnerable to XSS attacks.

Hardcoded database credentials 'postgres:postgres' in the database_url setting. Embedding database credentials in source code is a security risk if the code is committed to version control, shared, or deployed without overriding the setting.

Session signing secret is hardcoded as 'dev-only-change-me'. This weak/default secret allows an attacker to forge session tokens by computing valid signatures with the known secret, enabling session hijacking and impersonation of any user.

The password reset token is returned in the API response body ('reset_token': user.reset_token if user else None). This leaks the one-time reset token to the client, allowing anyone who intercepts the response to reset the user's password.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Cookie 'portal_crumb' is set without httponly, secure, or samesite flags. Without httponly, the cookie is accessible via JavaScript and can be stolen via XSS. Without secure, it is sent over HTTP. Without samesite, it is vulnerable to CSRF attacks.
